helpful: The provisioned document texts were decisive: the respondent file carried the merits brief as well as the BIO, and its table of authorities surfaced intervening OT2025 decisions (FCC v. AT&T, Sripetch) that postdate my training data and materially moved the forecast.
The statpack merits section's per-Term table with the excluded-count guard made the pooled baseline (359/515 over grant Terms 2017-2024) easy to compute and safe to quote.
gaps: The petitioner's merits brief (filed 2026-06-18, on the docket snapshot) was not provisioned even though the respondent's was; for a moment:grant merits cell the two sides' merits arguments have unequal standing in the record. Provisioning brief-on-the-merits kinds for both parties would remove the asymmetry.

fedcourts query has no doctrinal/topic filter usable on SCOTUS rows (the citation filter covers 161 of 590k rows), so finding 'similar Article III agency-adjudication merits cases' via the corpus is effectively impossible; a full-text or issue-tag filter would help merits cells.
A statpack cut of merits outcomes by petitioner type (SG petitions vs private) would give merits cells a conditioned anchor instead of an intuition.
